title: Bounded-below objects detect isomorphisms in sheaf derived categories
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Work in its ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Say $H$ is bounded below if $H^q(H)=0$ for all sufficiently negative $q$. If a morphism $\alpha:B\to G$ induces bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(H[n],B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H[n],G)$ for every bounded-below object $H$ and every $n\in\mathbf Z$, then $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. No boundedness hypothesis is imposed on $B$ or $G$.

proof.text: Complete $\alpha:B\to G$ to a distinguished triangle $B\xrightarrow{\alpha}G\xrightarrow{g}Z\xrightarrow{d}B[1]$. For any bounded-below $H$, transport the injectivity hypothesis at shift $-1$ through the adjunction $[-1]\dashv[1]$ to get injectivity of $\operatorname{Hom}(H,B[1])\to\operatorname{Hom}(H,G[1])$. Consecutive composites vanish, so for $f:H\to Z$ the composite $df$ has zero image in $\operatorname{Hom}(H,G[1])$, hence $df=0$. Exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(H,-)$ at $Z$, obtained by rotating the triangle once and using the cited Hom-exactness lemma, gives $f=gk$. The hypothesis at shift $0$ (transported along $H[0]\cong H$) lifts $k:H\to G$ to $l:H\to B$. Thus $f=g\alpha l=0$.

source.place: Tags 0146 (lemma-composition-zero), 0149 (lemma-representable-homological); elementary shift-adjunction transport and Hom chase

proof.text: Represent $Z$ by a complex $K$ with $QK\cong Z$. For each integer $q$ use the stupid lower truncation $L=\sigma_{\ge q-1}K$ and its actual inclusion $i:L\to K$. The object $QL$ is bounded below, so step 1 makes $Q(i):QL\to QK\cong Z$ zero. At degrees $q-1,q,q+1$ all terms are retained and the components of $i$ are isomorphisms. Consequently the induced map of the short complexes defining degree-$q$ cohomology is an isomorphism, hence $H^q(Q(i))$ is an isomorphism. This zero isomorphism has target $H^q(Z)$, which is therefore zero. This works for every $q$ and uses neither coproducts nor sequential colimits.

source.place: Tag 0118 (section-truncations), cochain stupid lower truncation; elementary comparison of the three retained terms defining cohomology

proof.text: Since every $H^q(Z)$ is zero, the zero endomorphism $0:Z\to Z$ induces an isomorphism on every cohomology object. The cohomology criterion for isomorphisms in the derived category implies that this zero endomorphism is invertible, whence $Z$ is zero. In a distinguished triangle the first arrow is an isomorphism exactly when the third object is zero, so $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. The latter elementary triangulated assertion is Mathlib Triangle.isZero₃_iff_isIso₁, proved using Hom exactness. Neither $B$ nor $G$ is assumed bounded.
